prompt: In the initial Discover, Offer, Request, ACK exchange, which TWO messages does the client send?
options: DHCPDISCOVER
DHCPOFFER
DHCPREQUEST
DHCPACK
explanation: The client sends Discover and Request. The server sends Offer and ACK.

whyWrong.1: An Offer comes from the server.
whyWrong.3: An ACK comes from the server.

prompt: A client receives a DHCPOFFER. What does that establish?
options: The client may use the address until the advertised lease expires.
A server has proposed configuration for the client.
The client has completed its duplicate-address check.
Every other server has withdrawn its offer.
explanation: An Offer is only a proposal. The client must still send a Request and receive an ACK before using the address.

whyWrong.0: The lease is not granted until the ACK.
whyWrong.2: An Offer does not complete any client checks.
whyWrong.3: Other servers learn of the choice from the client's Request.

prompt: A client with no address starts DHCPv4. What are the source and destination of its Discover?
options: 0.0.0.0 to the known default gateway
The proposed lease address to the offering server
The current lease address to 255.255.255.255
explanation: The client has no address and does not know a server, so it broadcasts from 0.0.0.0 to 255.255.255.255 using UDP 68 to 67.

whyWrong.1: The client has no gateway yet.
whyWrong.2: The offered address is not leased yet.
whyWrong.3: A client starting from scratch has no current lease address.

prompt: A lease expires without a successful renewal or rebinding. What must the client do?
options: Keep using it while the default gateway responds.
Stop using that lease and restart address acquisition.
Extend it locally for another original lease interval.
Keep using it until another client reports a duplicate.
explanation: When the lease expires, the client must stop using the address and start over with a Discover.

whyWrong.0: A working gateway does not extend a lease.
whyWrong.2: Only a server can extend a lease.
whyWrong.3: Duplicate reports do not extend a lease.

exhibit.title: Representative client settings
exhibit.text:
Autoconfiguration IPv4 Address : 169.254.87.14
Subnet Mask                  : 255.255.0.0
Default Gateway              :

prompt: A Windows client is set to obtain IPv4 settings automatically. What does this output show?
options: A normal routed DHCP lease is present, but its gateway is optional.
The relay failed; no server or client checks are necessary.
IPv4 link-local is in use; the intended DHCP configuration is absent.
The pool is exhausted; available-address checks are unnecessary.
explanation: A 169.254.0.0/16 address with no gateway is IPv4 link-local, which means the client got no DHCP lease.

whyWrong.0: A link-local address is not a routed DHCP lease.
whyWrong.1: The output does not show where the exchange failed.
whyWrong.3: Nothing here shows the pool is exhausted.

prompt: Which global command disables both the DHCP server and the DHCP relay on an IOS router?
options: no ip dhcp pool USERS
no ip domain-lookup
no ip dhcp excluded-address 10.10.10.1
no service dhcp
explanation: no service dhcp turns off both the IOS DHCP server and the relay. The service is on by default.

whyWrong.0: Removing a pool leaves the relay service on.
whyWrong.1: This disables DNS name lookup.

prompt: R1 receives client broadcasts on Gi0/0. The DHCP server is at 10.10.20.2 through Gi0/1. Where does ip helper-address go?
options: Under the DHCP pool on the remote server
On the server-facing Gi0/1 interface only
On every interface, including unused interfaces
On the client-facing Gi0/0 interface
explanation: Configure the helper on the interface that receives the client broadcasts, and point it at the server.

whyWrong.0: The pool does not receive or relay broadcasts.
whyWrong.1: Client broadcasts arrive on Gi0/0.
whyWrong.2: Only the client-facing interface needs it.

exhibit.title: Representative R1 configuration
exhibit.text:
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip address 10.10.10.1 255.255.255.0
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip address 10.10.20.1 255.255.255.0
 ip helper-address 10.10.20.2

prompt: A client on 10.10.10.0/24 cannot get a lease, and R1 has a helper on Gi0/1. What is the fix?
options: Move the helper from Gi0/1 to Gi0/0.
Set the client gateway option to 10.10.20.2.
Change Gi0/1's helper target to 10.10.10.1.
Change the pool network to 10.10.20.0/24.
explanation: The helper is on the server-facing interface. Client broadcasts arrive on Gi0/0, so the helper belongs there.

whyWrong.1: The gateway option is not the problem.
whyWrong.2: The helper must point at the server.
whyWrong.3: The pool must match the client subnet.

prompt: A relayed request arrives with giaddr 10.10.30.1. The server has pools for 10.10.20.0/24 and 10.10.30.0/24. Which pool serves the client?
options: Either pool, chosen only by its free-address count.
The 10.10.20.0/24 pool, matching the server interface.
The 10.10.30.0/24 pool, matching the relay's giaddr.
Neither pool, because giaddr must be zero.
explanation: The server uses giaddr to select the pool, so 10.10.30.1 selects the 10.10.30.0/24 pool.

whyWrong.0: The pool is chosen by giaddr, not free addresses.
whyWrong.1: The server's own subnet is not the client's subnet.
whyWrong.3: A relay sets giaddr to a nonzero value.

prompt: A client has a 12-hour lease with default timers. What happens at T1?
options: Broadcast a Discover immediately after three hours.
Stop using the address after six hours even if renewal succeeds.
Wait until all twelve hours have elapsed before contacting a server.
Attempt renewal with the leasing server by unicast after six hours.
explanation: T1 is 50% of the lease, so at 6 hours the client unicasts a renewal Request to the leasing server.

whyWrong.0: T1 is half the lease, not a quarter.
whyWrong.1: The client may keep the address while renewing.
whyWrong.2: The client renews well before expiry.

prompt: A fourth client's Discover reaches the server, but no address is offered. Why?
options: One candidate remains because the upper exclusion ends before .254.
No candidate remains because all three permitted host addresses are leased.
Two candidates remain because both exclusion endpoints are usable.
Three candidates remain because active bindings do not consume the pool.
explanation: The exclusions leave .50, .51 and .52, which are all leased, so no address is free.

whyWrong.0: .254 is excluded and .255 is the broadcast address.
whyWrong.2: Exclusion endpoints are included in the excluded range.
whyWrong.3: Active bindings use up the addresses.

prompt: A server shows 10.10.10.60 as a ping-detected conflict. What do you do before clearing it?
options: Clear .60 immediately because conflict entries cannot represent live hosts.
Clear every binding so the server can allocate a new address set.
Investigate who is using .60 and resolve the duplicate or stale condition.
Shorten the pool lease so the responding static host releases .60.
explanation: A conflict means another device answered for that address. Find the device and fix the duplicate before clearing the entry.

whyWrong.0: A live host can cause a conflict.
whyWrong.1: Clearing bindings can lead to duplicates.
whyWrong.3: A lease change does not release a static address.

exhibit.title: Representative request and configuration
exhibit.text:
Relayed DHCPDISCOVER: giaddr = 10.10.30.1
Configured dynamic pool networks:
 USERS  10.10.10.0 255.255.255.0
 SERVER 10.10.20.0 255.255.255.0

prompt: The relay and server paths work, but the request finds no pool. Why?
options: The server has no pool matching client subnet 10.10.30.0/24.
The server must use the pool with the greatest free capacity.
The relay must advertise its server-facing address as the client subnet.
The server must use its own connected subnet despite nonzero giaddr.
explanation: The server uses giaddr to find the client subnet, and it has no pool for 10.10.30.0/24.

whyWrong.1: Free addresses in another pool do not help.
whyWrong.2: giaddr must be the client-side address.
whyWrong.3: A nonzero giaddr selects the client subnet, not the server subnet.

prompt: A client moves to a new subnet and asks to reuse its old address. The server knows it is invalid there. Which message tells the client to give it up?
options: DHCPRELEASE
DHCPDECLINE
DHCPNAK
DHCPINFORM
explanation: A server sends DHCPNAK to reject an invalid request, and the client must restart.

whyWrong.0: DHCPRELEASE is sent by the client.
whyWrong.1: DHCPDECLINE is sent by the client.
whyWrong.3: DHCPINFORM is a client request for options.

prompt: A client has the right address, mask and gateway but DNS 10.10.20.99 instead of 10.10.20.53. What fixes this?
options: Correct the pool DNS option, then refresh the client's settings.
Correct only the router's ip name-server setting.
Clear only the client's cached DNS answers.
Reacquire the lease without correcting the pool option.
explanation: The DNS server comes from the pool's dns-server option. Correct it, then renew the client.

whyWrong.1: The router's resolver setting is not what clients receive.
whyWrong.2: Clearing the cache does not change the resolver address.
whyWrong.3: The pool would give the same wrong value.

prompt: A server answers a client on its own subnet with giaddr and ciaddr zero and the BROADCAST flag set. How does it send the Offer or ACK?
options: Unicast to the offered client IPv4 address.
Broadcast the Offer or ACK.
Unicast to the relay gateway address.
Unicast to the client's current IPv4 address.
explanation: With giaddr and ciaddr zero and the broadcast flag set, the server broadcasts the reply.

whyWrong.0: The broadcast flag selects broadcast delivery.
whyWrong.2: giaddr is zero, so there is no relay.
whyWrong.3: ciaddr is zero, so there is no current address.

prompt: The dynamic range is 10.8.0.10 to 10.8.0.29 in 10.8.0.0/27. Which exclusions produce it?
explanation: The hosts are .1 to .30. Excluding .1 to .9 and .30 leaves .10 to .29.

whyWrong.0: This excludes .29.
whyWrong.1: This excludes .10 and .29.

prompt: A client is past T2 with no renewal reply and its lease has not expired. What does it do?
options: Broadcast Request while retaining the still-valid leased address.
Send Request only to the original server and ignore other servers.
Use Discover with source 0.0.0.0 and immediately discard the lease.
Use Release to ask all available servers to extend the lease.
explanation: At rebinding (T2), the client broadcasts a Request to any server and keeps using the address until the lease expires.

whyWrong.1: That describes renewal at T1.
whyWrong.2: The client does not give up the lease before expiry.
whyWrong.3: Release gives up an address and does not ask for an extension.

prompt: A server excludes 10.8.0.20, and a printer should always use .20. What does the exclusion do alone?
options: It reserves .20 for whichever printer requests first.
It creates a manual binding for the printer's client identifier.
It configures .20 directly on the printer's interface.
It prevents this server's dynamic pool from offering .20.
explanation: An exclusion stops the dynamic pool from offering the address. It does not assign it to anyone.

whyWrong.0: It does not reserve the address for a client.
whyWrong.1: A manual binding is a separate configuration.
whyWrong.2: The server does not configure the printer.

prompt: The server shows an active binding for a test client. What further check shows the client uses the intended configuration?
options: Inspect only the total server allocation counter.
Treat the binding alone as proof that the client received the ACK.
Verify its actual address/options and test the required service.
Compare only the configured lease duration with the design.
explanation: A server binding does not prove the client received it. Check the client's address and options, then test the service.

whyWrong.0: A counter does not show one client's settings.
whyWrong.1: A binding alone does not show the ACK arrived.
whyWrong.3: The lease length says nothing about delivery.

prompt: A client gets 10.50.0.60/24 with gateway 10.50.0.99, but the approved gateway is .1. Local tests work and routed ones fail. What is the fix?
options: Change the DHCP pool network to the DNS resolver's subnet.
Correct default-router to .1, refresh the client, and retest routed service.
Remove the client-subnet exclusion protecting the router's address.
Correct only the DNS option and repeat a name lookup.
explanation: The client has the wrong default gateway. Correct default-router to .1 and renew the client.

whyWrong.0: The client is already on the correct subnet.
whyWrong.2: The router address should stay excluded.
whyWrong.3: The DNS setting is already correct.

prompt: The server receives a Discover and sends an Offer to the relay. The client never receives an Offer. Which TWO faults fit?
options: The path from server to relay drops the reply.
The server has no matching pool and therefore never sent an Offer.
The relay-to-client delivery path drops the Offer.
The client successfully received and accepted this Offer.
explanation: The server sent the Offer, so the loss is on the path to the relay or from the relay to the client.

whyWrong.1: The Offer was sent, so a pool matched.
whyWrong.3: The client never received an Offer.

exhibit.title: Representative teaching evidence
exhibit.text:
R1: Gi0/0 10.30.0.1/24, helper 10.20.0.2; Gi0/1 10.20.0.1/24
R2: 10.20.0.2/24; service dhcp enabled; pool 10.30.0.0/24 has free addresses
R2 routes: connected 10.20.0.0/24; no default or other route
Current request at R2: giaddr 10.30.0.1; Offer prepared for relay
R1 ping 10.20.0.2: success

prompt: The server prepares an Offer, but the fresh client still gets none. What is missing?
options: The relay needs another helper on its server-facing interface.
The server needs a route toward the nonzero giaddr.
The client needs a static address before sending Discover.
The pool must match the server's connected subnet.
explanation: The server replies toward giaddr 10.30.0.1 and has no route to it. Add a route back to the client subnet through R1.

whyWrong.0: The Discover already arrived through the relay.
whyWrong.2: A client with no address is the normal DHCP case.
whyWrong.3: The pool already matches the client subnet.

exhibit.title: Representative teaching evidence
exhibit.text:
R1 guest Gi0/2: 10.40.0.1/24, helper 10.20.0.2
R1 users Gi0/0: 10.30.0.1/24, helper 10.20.0.2
R2 service-side address 10.20.0.2/24; peer R1 10.20.0.1
R2 only pool: USERS 10.30.0.0/24, free candidates available
R2 only remote route: 10.30.0.0/24 via 10.20.0.1
Guest Discover reaches R2 with giaddr 10.40.0.1

prompt: A new guest VLAN needs leases without breaking existing users. Which TWO changes are needed?
options: Add a 10.40.0.0/24 pool with guest gateway 10.40.0.1.
Move the existing USERS pool from 10.30.0.0/24 to 10.40.0.0/24.
Add a server return route for 10.40.0.0/24 via 10.20.0.1.
Replace the guest helper target with 10.40.0.1.
Remove exclusions from the already working USERS pool.
explanation: The new subnet needs its own pool and a server route back to its relay. Leave USERS and the working helper alone.

whyWrong.1: Moving USERS would break the existing subnet.
whyWrong.3: The helper must point at the server.
whyWrong.4: Exclusions in USERS do not serve the guest subnet.

exhibit.title: Representative teaching evidence
exhibit.text:
Five clients retain unexpired leases and reach the remote application.
After a relay change, one newly connected PC has no valid lease.
No current server or packet evidence has yet been collected.

prompt: Which test best separates a current DHCP failure from a client still using an old lease?
options: Clear every lease and infer success if existing clients reconnect.
Ping the default gateway only from a client with an unexpired lease.
Request a lease from a fresh client while correlating relay/server evidence.
Shorten every lease and wait until users report a new outage.
explanation: A client with an unexpired lease can keep working even when allocation fails. Test with a fresh client and check the relay and server.

whyWrong.0: Clearing leases disrupts healthy clients.
whyWrong.1: A ping from a leased client tests no new allocation.
whyWrong.3: Changing timers is disruptive and less direct.

prompt: Which UDP port does a DHCPv4 server listen on?
explanation: DHCPv4 servers listen on UDP 67 and clients use UDP 68.

whyWrong.0: 53 is DNS.
whyWrong.3: 123 is NTP.

prompt: At what fraction of the lease does a DHCP client rebind (T2) by default?
explanation: The default T2 is 87.5% of the lease. T1 (renewal) is 50%.

whyWrong.0: 50% is T1, the renewal time.
whyWrong.1: 75% is not a default timer.
whyWrong.3: 100% is lease expiry.

prompt: What is the default lease time on an IOS DHCP pool?
options: 1 hour
8 hours
1 day
7 days
explanation: The default IOS lease is one day.

whyWrong.0: 1 hour is not the default.
whyWrong.1: 8 hours is not the default.
whyWrong.3: 7 days is not the default.

prompt: What administrative distance does the default route learned by ip address dhcp have?
explanation: A default route learned through ip address dhcp has administrative distance 254.

whyWrong.0: 1 is a static route.
whyWrong.1: 110 is OSPF.
whyWrong.3: 255 means the route is unusable.
